title: If It Rains...: ha + Present Tense

sections.title: No special "if" tense needed
sections.content: To talk about what you'll do depending on the weather, use ha ("if") with the present tense in both halves of the sentence — Hungarian doesn't need a special future or conditional form here, the present tense alone carries the meaning: Ha esik az eső, otthon maradok. ("If it rains, I'll stay home.") The ha-clause usually comes first, followed by a comma.

items.spanish: Ha esik az eső, otthon maradok.
items.english: If it rains, I'll stay home.

items.spanish: Ha szép idő van, a parkba megyünk.
items.english: If the weather's nice, we'll go to the park.
If it's cold, I'll put on a coat.

sections.content: You can also flip the order — Otthon maradok, ha esik az eső. — the ha-clause just needs ha and the present tense, wherever it sits in the sentence.
